scope.description: Short focused follow-up of four historical entities and their strongest discoverable leads. This was not a new search of all 98 remaining health subjects.

findings.outcome: Promising primary advertisement lead located; no downloadable and visually verified artwork accepted.

sources.outcome: Official Canadian Nurse archive indexed as containing the decade’s print issues. Direct HTTP retrieval and web retrieval both returned 403.

sources.urlNote: Stable object identity only. Discovery URL contained an expired signed query; that complete indexed signed URL returned 403. No unsigned-access result is claimed.
sources.outcome: Indexed OCR identifies Thompson Health Region, Kamloops, BC recruitment advertisement for Director, Prevention and Early Intervention, Public Health, with tagline A Path to Better Health. The scan itself could not be downloaded or visually verified; issue date and artwork geometry remain unconfirmed.
Retrieved historical council minutes, May 30, 2000. Text mentions Thompson Health Region Sun Sense delegation, but does not supply attributable agency artwork. No mark accepted.

exclusions: David Thompson Health Region is an Alberta organization; its mountain/DTHR logo was not assigned to the BC Thompson Health Region.
Current Interior Health identity is a successor and was not used to fill this gap.
findings.recommendedRoute: Retrieve the original Canadian Nurse issue through its official archive or a public-library periodical copy; search the exact recruitment job title and tagline, establish the issue date, and inspect/extract the actual printed logo. The dated Merritt agenda correspondence is a separate useful municipal-archive request.

findings.outcome: Historical newspaper lead remains inaccessible at the old file URL; successor identity excluded.

sources.outcome: Retrieved 680 bytes of text/html titled fallthrough, a migration application shell rather than PDF. Therefore no publication was visually inspected or extracted.

Official library page identifies Biblioboard as the current digital collection and says newspapers cover 1948–2001. This is a verified replacement archive route, not proof that the specific issue contains a logo.

exclusions: The repository already holds the 2001 teal website GIF of Coast Garibaldi Community Health Services Society. Its attribution does not establish ownership by the earlier Regional Health Board.
The previously inspected 2000 arsenic report did not establish an attributable board logo; it was not reclassified.
findings.recommendedRoute: Open the 1996-09-17 Squamish Chief issue in the library’s Biblioboard collection, then inspect health-board recruitment/public-notice advertisements.1996-02-27 and 1996-12-03 indexed issues provide additional exact-name context but were not visually inspected in this pass.

findings.outcome: Focused exact-name searches found primary name-only records, not recoverable original artwork.

sources.outcome: Indexed primary public-account payment table names the society. Text-only payment references were not counted as logo evidence. PDF graphics were not inspected in this short pass.
Primary legal record identifies society appointments. It is organizational context, not artwork.

findings.recommendedRoute: Locate 1997–2001 society-authored annual reports, letterhead or recruitment notices in Prince Rupert/Terrace public-library newspaper holdings and provincial archival catalogues. Inspect original documents before attributing any mark; keep the earlier North West Regional Health Board separate. No specific archival holding is asserted.

findings.outcome: Focused exact-name searches found name-only primary reports/legal records; no attributable artwork accepted.

sources.outcome: Indexed primary audit table lists the society among audited entities, but the table supplies no attributable society artwork. Full publication was not visually inspected in this short pass.
Primary legal record identifies society appointments. It is organizational context, not artwork.

exclusions: East Kootenay Foundation for Health is a different organization; its current logo was not assigned to the former society.
Interior Health successor branding and the separate East Kootenay Regional Health Board were not substituted.
findings.recommendedRoute: Seek 1997–2001 society annual reports and correspondence in Cranbrook-area public-library/municipal archives or provincial health-record collections. Agency-authored recruitment advertisements may contain the original signature. This recommendation is an archival strategy, not a verified catalogue holding.

conclusion: No newly accepted asset from this bounded pass. All 98 atlas-health gaps remain unchanged. Failed retrievals, indexed OCR, entity mentions and successor marks were not treated as collected artwork.
